Installing the Mwakete SMS app

The Mwakete SMS app sends your campaigns from your own phone and SIM. Because it is installed straight onto the phone — not from the Google Play Store — Android’s Play Protect will usually warn about it, and on newer phones may block it at first. That is normal for any app that can send texts, not a sign the app is unsafe. This page shows how to install it. The app only sends the messages you press Start on at Mwakete.com; it never reads your personal texts — the one thing it notices is a reply of STOP, so that person is taken off your list.

Before you start

  • An Android phone (Android 7 or newer) with the SIM you want to send from.
  • The app file. On SMS → Phones & SIMs → Connect an Android phone, tap the download the Mwakete SMS app link.
  • Contacts & SMS switched on for your store (ask Mwakete if the SMS page says it is off).

Step 1 — Let the phone install it

Open the downloaded file. The first time, Android says it cannot install apps from this place.

  1. Tap Settings on that message.
  2. Turn on Allow from this source (for the app you downloaded with — Chrome, or Files).
  3. Go back and tap Install.

Step 2 — If Play Protect blocks it

If you see “Unsafe app blocked”, “App scan recommended”, or it simply will not install and there is no Install anyway, turn the Play Protect scan off just long enough to install:

  1. Open the Play Store app.
  2. Tap your profile picture (top right).
  3. Tap Play Protect, then the gear / Settings in the corner.
  4. Turn off “Scan apps with Play Protect”.
  5. Go back and install the Mwakete SMS app.
  6. When it is installed, turn Play Protect back on.

This is safe to do for your own tool on your own phone. You are only pausing the scan while you install an app you trust.

Step 3 — Connect it

  1. Open the app and allow the text-message and phone permissions it asks for — it needs these to send from your SIM.
  2. On Mwakete.com (SMS → Phones & SIMs) press Get a code, and type that code into the app within 10 minutes.
  3. Your SIM now shows under Phones & SIMs. Leave the app open (or in the background) when a campaign is due.

Why the warning appears

Google shows this warning for every app that can send SMS and is installed from outside the Play Store. The Mwakete app cannot go on the Play Store because Google only allows texting apps there if they are your phone’s main messaging app — so it is installed directly instead, and the warning comes with that. The app sends only your campaigns, from your SIM, under your carrier’s terms.

Updating the app later

When a newer version is posted, download it and install over the old one — your connection stays. If it says “App not installed”, uninstall the old Mwakete SMS first, then install the new one and connect again with a fresh code.

Still stuck?

  • Can’t find Play Protect? It lives inside the Play Store, under your profile picture — not in the phone’s main Settings.
  • A work or school phone? Some are locked so no outside apps can be installed at all. Use a personal phone for the SIM instead.
  • No Play Store on the phone? Then Play Protect is not the blocker — check Step 1 (Allow from this source).
